response.sql: SELECT original_language_id, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY original_language_id ORDER BY films DESC, original_language_id IS NULL, original_language_id LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The database is MySQL (the Sakila schema), where GROUP BY places all NULL original_language_id rows into one group and `ORDER BY ... IS NULL` is valid.

"Any missing counts last" is read as placing the no-language group after other groups with the same film count. Film counts are never missing, so this is the only place a missing value can affect the order.

"Ignoring missing values" in the average is a no-op here, because rental_rate and rental_duration are both NOT NULL. The average is left unrounded, and replacement_cost > 20.99 is a strict comparison.

alternatives.interpretation: Place the no-language group last regardless of its film count, and sort all other groups by film count from most to fewest.
alternatives.sql: SELECT original_language_id, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY original_language_id ORDER BY original_language_id IS NULL, films DESC, original_language_id LIMIT 10;
